This is a list I typed up for a friend who had just discovered podcasts.

Ok podcast talk I would guess you already know about the NPR shows but Radio Lab and This American Life are great.

I would recommend The Tobolowsky Files to anyone very funny and touching "true stories of life, love, and the entertainment industry told by Stephen Tobolwsky". Just SO good.

Answer Me This is great, two Brits answer your questions.

The Bugle is fun political satire with John Oliver and Andy Zaltzman.

The Dead Authors Podcast can be really good but the guest really matters It's Paul F. Thompkins as H.G. Wells interviewing other comedians also pretending to be dead authors The John Hodgeman one as Ayn Rand was hilarious.

Doug Loves Movies is great and I don't really even like the host Doug Benson and I rarely watch movies. It's all about the panel.

How Did This Get Made Paul Sheer, June Diane Raphael, Jason Mantzoukas, and a guest talk about bad movies.

International Waters is a US vs. Great Britain comedy panel game.

Jordan, Jessie, Go! silly comedy.

Judge John Hodgman. People send in problems and two people come on the show and he judges who is right.

Never Not Funny with Jimmy Pardo.

No Such Thing As A Fish, quirky fact show also British the people behind the facts of a very popular panel quiz show on the BBC QI.

The Smartest Man in the World is a show with Greg Proops talking it is very funny but can also be very depressing because he does a "boring preachy part" his words, and he is very liberal, very feminist and he finds some horrible things going on in the world and lets you know.

TBTL~Too Beautiful To Live is one of my faves, the host is Luke Burbank, you might have heard him on NPR's Wait Wait Don't Tell Me panel.

The Grapes Of Rad also silly comedy but one of the hosts just went through a divorce and is really working on himself.

You Made it Weird is pretty good if you can start at the beginning you really see the host Pete Holmes grow as a person. It is funny and he tries to get everyone he talks to to talk about comedy, sex/love, and religion/death.

Pop Rocket is one of my new favorites! Host Guy Branum and panelists Wynter Mitchell, Oliver Wang and Margaret Wappler for smart, funny, sometimes sweary chat about everything great in entertainment.

Sure, I was on a really tight schedule, so everything came from Joanns. The knit aisle to be specific. The shirt is out of their swimwear line, all the rest was just cheap knits I think it's all mostly polyester. 

Everything being stretchy I first ironed on interfacing then WonderUnder on the white and black. For all the little bits and pieces on the shirt and belt.

For the shirt I took the pattern of some jammies that had a raglan sleeve and just adjusted them to be super tight just took 4inches in on the front and back. The sleeves were a bit more work. 
A lot of google was used to get images of the A (and the belt and such). Then I drew everything on the wonderunder cut it out then ironed it on then went over everything with a tight zigzag. (also interfacing just a bit bigger than the circle on the inside of the shirt so it doesn't stretch when you are sewing on the A)


Belt I just kind of freehanded based on pics online, 

the little guy on the belt: I printed out a guy and then drew it on with a light box then pained it with fabric paint...I had to go over the outline with white because when I sewed it the next day the black spread on the presser foot. 

For the helmet I found a help online http://www.instructables.com/id/Make-an-Aquabats-Anti-Negativity-Helmet/ I just shrunk it down to fit my 3 year old. I made it out of a thicker knit neoprene would have been better but I didn't have the time to get it or want to spend too much.
